chapter: Early career: vaudeville and Kansas City
title: Debut as accompanist: nightclubs rather than vaudeville pits
summary: Basie disputes Feather's 'professional debut in New York accompanying vaudeville acts', saying he accompanied acts in nightclubs but never played a theater pit, and refuses to name early gigs.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Okay. "Professional debut in New York as accompanist to vaudeville acts."
What did you say?
"Professional debut in New York as accompanist to vaudeville acts." That's Chapter Four, right? Is that so? Were you playing for vaudeville acts in New York?
That's before (inaudible) going to where? (Inaudible)
I guess --
Read that.
"Professional debut in New York as accompanist to vaudeville acts." So you were playing piano or organ for vaudeville acts in New York? No.
Well, I don't think that -- I think they got Some of that... (Inaudible). What's just before that?

Well, nothing, except that you were studying informally with Fats Waller, so what Leonard Feather is saying here is that the first time you played professionally, you played in New York, accompanying vaudeville acts. But he doesn't say whether it's piano or organ. And he doesn't give a date.
Well, I don't know how to just go through all this. I mean, I don't -- I hate to just do anything about how? He's got the thing written there.
Well, I mean, he probably just didn't have much to go on, you know, so it's not as if he was, you know, getting out of -- I suppose he just picked this up, you know?
Yeah, well, I mean, I did work at different vaudeville -- I worked a couple of vaudeville acts, but I don't think that's -- that was my debut. Isn't that what he called it, debut?
Yeah, right.
That -- not, it was (inaudible) quite a while before I could get to that point. We were in New York a little while before that happened.
Oh.
I was (inaudible) before (inaudible) other things and maybe that's (inaudible) vaudeville acts. I mean, (inaudible).
I don't know. Theaters, I guess.
He would have to be in the theater, playing the theater --
Yeah.
-- to do that (inaudible).
I guess it would be something, what? Like the Lafayette or --
No, we never worked the Lafayette, only Benny Moten's band. with (inaudible)

Well, I mean, I don't even know -- from what this says, I don't even know, you know, if you were alone accompanying. It sounds as if you were alone, you know, you weren't with a group or band or something.
Well, that's -- well, he's half right. But he just don't know who.
He's half right in the sense that --
I did play in vaudeville acts.
In New York?
Well, it's not only in New York. I mean, you could accompany me singers and things like that in a nightclub, but you'd had to work --
I see.
-- you'd had to work in a theater to accompany vaudeville acts.
That's what I mean. Well, did you --
You'd have to work in a pit there or something like that. I never worked at a pit in a theater in New York.
So that you were doing -- you were rather accompanying in nightclubs in New York before you would have been in theaters. Is that so?
That's right.
I see. Do you want to get into that?
You can, I mean, get into that, but I can't -- I'm not going to tell you where and how.
You're not going to tell me --
-- because, I mean, they were -- there were different clubs that started me, how I got in, how I got to New York --
Yeah.
-- where I went, my first job, first gigs in there --
Yeah.
-- and the first gigs for me to start, what started in vaudeville and who -- what -- you call them groups now. We called them combinations then and things like that --
Right. And you don't want to get into that then?
Not really, baby.
